title: Whales originated from aquatic artiodactyls in the Eocene epoch of India
authors: Thewissen, J.G.M.; Cooper, L.N.; Clementz, M.T.; Bajpai, S.; Tiwari, B.N.
note: The study combines separately catalogued skull, limb-bone histology and tooth-isotope samples from the Sindkhatudi bone bed; it does not describe one associated skeleton or a direct cetacean ancestor.

title: Skeletons of terrestrial cetaceans and the relationship of whales to artiodactyls
authors: Thewissen, J.G.M.; Williams, E.M.; Roe, L.J.; Hussain, S.T.
note: The Pakicetus reconstruction is a locality-level composite of separately catalogued postcranial bones plus skull H-GSP 96231, not an associated skeleton from one individual.

title: Fossil evidence for the origin of aquatic locomotion in archaeocete whales
authors: Thewissen, J.G.M.; Hussain, S.T.; Arif, M.
note: Holotype H-GSP 18507 from the Kuldana Formation supplies the partial skeleton used for the original locomotor reconstruction.

title: An amphibious whale from the middle Eocene of Peru reveals early South Pacific dispersal of quadrupedal cetaceans
authors: Lambert, O.; Bianucci, G.; Salas-Gismondi, R.; et al.
note: Holotype MUSM 3580 is tied to the lowest Yumaque Member and an approximately 42.6 Ma nannofossil age; locomotion and dispersal route are explicitly analytical interpretations.

title: Hind limbs of Eocene Basilosaurus: evidence of feet in whales
authors: Gingerich, P.D.; Smith, B.H.; Simons, E.L.
note: The original report describes Egyptian Basilosaurus isis pelvic limbs and feet; the proposed copulatory role is a functional interpretation, not observed behaviour.

title: Transition of Eocene whales from land to sea: evidence from bone microstructure
authors: Houssaye, A.; Tafforeau, P.; de Muizon, C.; Gingerich, P.D.
note: Table 1 and Figure 11 identify the scanned male Basilosaurus isis femur as UM 93231; tissue compactness is measured, while locomotor interpretation remains comparative.

title: Aegicetus gehennae, a new late Eocene protocetid (Cetacea, Archaeoceti) from Wadi Al Hitan, Egypt, and the transition to tail-powered swimming in whales
authors: Gingerich, P.D.; Antar, M.S.M.; Zalmout, I.S.
note: Holotype CGM 60584 and referred specimen CGM 60583 come from the lower Gehannam Formation; the paper discloses a Bartonian–Priabonian age conflict and treats tail propulsion as a functional inference.

title: Correction: Aegicetus gehennae, a new late Eocene protocetid and the transition to tail-powered swimming in whales
note: Publisher correction retained beside the primary paper so corrected table and figure material remains discoverable.

title: Phylogenetic relationships among cetartiodactyls based on insertions of short and long interspersed elements: Hippopotamuses are the closest extant relatives of whales
authors: Nikaido, M.; Rooney, A.P.; Okada, N.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: The study characterizes 16 new independent retropositional events at 10 loci and analyses 20 informative events across its combined data matrix.

title: Divergence date estimation and a comprehensive molecular tree of extant cetaceans
authors: McGowen, M.R.; Spaulding, M.; Gatesy, J.
note: The 42,335-character supermatrix samples 87 of 89 cetacean species recognized by the authors in 2009; it is a historical molecular model, not the current COL26.8 catalogue.
